_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 11. Blau notes consulted: 11:4 (ראסה ידאני אלסמא = 'its top approaches close to the sky' — Saadia softens 'בשמים'); 11:5, 11:7 (אמרא מוגהא = 'a directed command' — Saadia's signature anti-anthropomorphic substitution for וירד ה'); 11:7 (לכנא = 1pl 'but we' — Cairo follows the divine plural). v.28, 31 'אתון אלכסדאניין' = 'the furnace of the Chaldeans' (Saadia interprets 'אור כשדים' as a furnace, not as the place name Ur — preserving the rabbinic tradition of Abram and the furnace). v.26 Cairo prints 'אברהם' but elsewhere in Gen 11-16 it's 'אברם'; standardizing to 'Abram' until the Gen 17 renaming.

translations.1: And all the dwellers of the earth were of one language and one speech.
translations.2: And when they had journeyed from the east, they found a valley in the land of Shinar; and they settled there.
translations.3: And one to another they said: 'Come, let us mold bricks, and bake them by firing.' And the brick was for them as stone, and the bitumen was for them as mortar.
translations.4: They said: 'Come, let us build for ourselves a town, and a tower whose top approaches close to the sky; and let us make for ourselves names, lest we be scattered upon the face of all the earth.'
translations.5: And God sent down a directed command, to look upon the town and the tower which the children of Adam had begun to build.
translations.6: And God said: 'Behold, they are as one people, and one language for them all; and this is what they have begun to do; and now, nothing will be beyond them — all that they have set their minds to do.
translations.7: Yet we shall send down a directed command, that by it we may scatter their languages, so that each group shall not hear the language of its fellow.'
translations.8: And God scattered them from there upon the face of all the earth; and they ceased from building the town.
translations.9: Therefore it was named Babel — for there God scattered the language of all the dwellers of the earth; and from there God dispersed them upon the whole face of it.
translations.10: This is the exposition of the offspring of Shem. When Shem was a son of a hundred years, he begot Arpachshad — two years after the flood.
translations.11: And Shem lived after that five hundred years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.12: And when Arpachshad had lived thirty-five years, he begot Shelah.
translations.13: And Arpachshad lived after that four hundred and three years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.14: And when Shelah had lived thirty years, he begot Eber.
translations.15: And Shelah lived after that four hundred and three years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.16: And when Eber had lived thirty-four years, he begot Peleg.
translations.17: And Eber lived after that four hundred and thirty years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.18: And when Peleg had lived thirty years, he begot Reu.
translations.19: And Peleg lived after that two hundred and nine years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.20: And when Reu had lived thirty-two years, he begot Serug.
translations.21: And Reu lived after that two hundred and seven years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.22: And when Serug had lived thirty years, he begot Nahor.
translations.23: And Serug lived after that two hundred years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.24: And when Nahor had lived twenty-nine years, he begot Terah.
translations.25: And Nahor lived after that a hundred and nineteen years, in which he begot sons and daughters.
translations.26: And when Terah had lived seventy years, he begot Abram, and Nahor, and Haran.
translations.27: And this is the exposition of the offspring of Terah, for he begot Abram, and Nahor, and Haran; and Haran begot Lot.
translations.28: And Haran died in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in the furnace of the Chaldeans.
translations.29: And Abram and Nahor took for themselves wives. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor's wife was Milkah, daughter of Haran, father of Milkah and father of Yiskah.
translations.30: And Sarai was barren; she had no child.
translations.31: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, the son of his son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram his son; and they went forth with them from the furnace of the Chaldeans, to go to the land of Canaan; and they came to Haran, and settled there.
translations.32: And the lifetime of Terah was two hundred and five years; and he died in Haran.
